response.markdown_report:
### Insights

**Starting point.** (1) Electronics’ sampled negative-wins rate is 9.7%, versus 1.32% for CDs_and_Vinyl. This supports category-specific investigation, not validation conclusions. (2) Embedding scores near 0.5 indicate approximately zero mean cosine. Collapse regularization lacks supporting evidence. (3) Feedback suggests older interests may distract from recent behavior. Prefix removal tests this hypothesis without inferring ownership, compatibility requirements, or purchase readiness.

**Related work.** (1) *Does It Look Sequential?* motivates separating recency from order sensitivity [1]. Retaining chronological suffixes preserves that distinction. (2) Recency sampling changes target exposure [2]; CL4SRec adds contrastive supervision [4]. Neither establishes a suffix-length optimum. (3) Sampled rankings and adaptive validation selection have distinct limitations [3,6]. Training margins remain diagnostic; fixed host macro HR@10 selects the condition.

### Directions and framework

Three directions remain: context intervention, supervision control, and ranking measurement.

| Condition | Recurrent context | Supervised positions |
|---|---|---|
| A: baseline | Full | All valid |
| B: matched control | Full | Retained suffix |
| C: prefix removal | Retained suffix | Same as B |

C−B estimates the training-policy effect of removing context under matched supervision; B−A estimates supervision-policy effects. Neither identifies a psychological mechanism.

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Matched prefix removal: 4/7/4.** Originality: useful controlled combination, although cropping is established. Potential: reusable context experiment, although benefits remain unmeasured. Difficulty: small masks, although candidate matching and padding require care [1,2,4,5].
- **Old-prefix shuffling: 4/6/3.** Originality: isolates older order, although follows existing perturbations. Potential: separates order from recency, although histories may become unrealistic. Difficulty: straightforward permutations, although supervision must remain matched [1].
- **Jointly learned recurrent decay: 5/7/6.** Originality: integrates recency within one GRU, although decay gates are established. Potential: adaptive retention, although sparse histories limit identification. Difficulty: compact parameters, although architecture/predictor synchronization adds debugging.

### Selected idea: matched prefix removal

At 20% progress, retain the first idea. Lower its originality/potential ratings and raise difficulty to reflect established augmentation and implementation controls.

```python
sequence, positive, negative = sample_batch(...)
keep = suffix_mask(sequence, p=0.5, alpha=0.5, rng=crop_rng)
context = sequence * keep if condition == 'C' else sequence
supervise = valid if condition == 'A' else valid & keep
features = model.log2feats(context)
loss = baseline_loss(features, positive, negative, supervise)
```

For n real inputs, retain n with probability 1−p; otherwise draw K uniformly from ceil(αn)…n. Keep the last K inputs and aligned original targets. Single-item histories remain unchanged. This policy is a hypothesis; freeze it without tuning.

Match B/C initialization, batches, negatives, masks, candidate handling, loss semantics, regularization and reduction. Reset recurrent state per example; skip padding updates and preserve retained-step gradients [5]. Verify padding invariance, batched/single equivalence, state isolation and finite nonzero gradients. Read the final nonpadding position, never count−1. Inference uses complete permitted histories.

Predeclare twelve category-condition runs, a common affordable epoch count ≤200, 200 batches/epoch, final-checkpoint selection and A→B→C tie-breaking. Preserve seeds, routing, predictor consistency and diagnostic interfaces. Track all GPU expenditure within 43,200 seconds [8]. Select one complete condition by macro validation HR@10; deploy one checkpoint/category without fusion. Report paired hit/miss changes and within-category paired-bootstrap macro intervals when available; these exclude training randomness, candidate variability and selection bias [6,7]. No improvement is claimed before evaluation.

References: [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12008), [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643), [3](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/), [4](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.14395), [5](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf), [6](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html), [7](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.03098), [8](https://aclanthology.org/D19-1224/).

idea.description: Evaluate stochastic old-prefix removal in corrected GRU4Rec through three separate conditions: unchanged baseline A, full-context training with suffix-only supervision B, and cropped-context training with identical suffix supervision C. Freeze one explicit cropping policy, compare complete conditions using four-category macro validation HR@10, and deploy exactly one independently trained checkpoint per category from the selected condition.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback suggests older interactions may distract from recent interests, but sampled training margins do not establish that mechanism or validation ranking quality. Matching supervised targets and candidates separates the context-removal training policy from supervision allocation. At 20% research progress, this controlled experiment is more practical than adding learned recurrent decay. Cropping may also regularize the model rather than specifically remove stale interests; improved HR@10 alone cannot distinguish these explanations.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve the supplied corrected GRU4Rec backbone, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, all four datasets, splits, host evaluator and DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']. Write all artifacts beneath the trial directory. Do not inspect other trials, reuse checkpoints, fetch pretrained weights, access hidden tests or modify host evaluation. Each run uses one GPU; four concurrent slots do not multiply the shared 43,200 GPU-second allowance.

Before examining condition results, declare twelve category-condition runs, one common epoch count E<=200 affordable within the remaining budget, and final-epoch checkpoint selection. Determine feasibility using host-provided timing or a charged baseline timing measurement; count every attempted run, failure, diagnostic and evaluation. Keep baseline optimizer, loss and other hyperparameters unchanged. If the complete comparison cannot fit, report the limitation rather than making an unmatched comparison. Use exact macro HR@10 values for selection; break equal scores by A, then B, then C. Do not tune p or alpha in this experiment. Log per-condition expenditure and best-so-far macro HR@10 against cumulative GPU-seconds only when complete four-category scores exist.

For n nonpadding inputs, retain all n with probability 0.5; otherwise sample integer K uniformly from max(1,ceil(0.5*n)) through n, inclusive. Retain the last K nonpadding positions without reordering, preserving their original aligned positive and negative IDs. Empty rows contribute no supervised loss; single-item histories are unchanged. The inclusive upper bound means the realized probability of removing context is below 0.5. Masking earlier losses in B leaves their inputs and gradient paths available to later retained targets; C removes those earlier inputs. Both retain target adjacency for every supervised position. Use full permitted histories at inference, with no cropping.

Use dedicated deterministic generators for crop masks, base batches and negative sampling; initialize these identically across conditions and categories as appropriate to the supplied seed-42 baseline. Do not let crop draws alter model/dropout or base-sampling RNG streams. Match B/C initial parameters, base samples, target frequencies, negative IDs/counts/distribution, duplicate and accidental-positive handling, score activation, temperature, sampling corrections, regularization, optimizer/scheduler steps and loss denominator. Inspect the actual supplied loss and sampler during implementation: do not replace them with presumed BPR, BPR-max or cross-entropy semantics. If negatives are pooled from supervised targets, construct the same pool in B/C. Preserve A's reduction exactly; define B/C reductions identically, preferably averaging valid supervised positions if compatible with the supplied objective. Document any difference from A. Equal targets and updates do not imply equal gradient magnitudes or optimization trajectories.

Zero embeddings do not prevent GRU padding updates. Preserve correct baseline padding handling; otherwise compact real tokens and right-pad internally before packing, or mask every recurrent layer's state update. If a correction is necessary, apply it uniformly before the comparison and synchronize the predictor. Reset state for every independent example and preserve gradients through every retained step. Restore aligned B x L x H outputs for log2feats. Read the final nonpadding position using the maximum valid index, never count-1; handle empty histories according to the supplied baseline. Check extra-left-padding score invariance, batched versus unpadded single-example equivalence, no cross-example state leakage, finite nonzero gradients on retained embeddings and recurrent parameters, and checkpoint/predictor score agreement.

Preserve item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), ModelView and view.model as the actual trained nn.Module. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis); return measured metrics and metric_definitions, preserve model mode and handle batches (None, sequence, positive, negative). Use fixed diagnostic snapshots and candidate pairs where available, retaining padding/context checks, measurement counts, history-length strata and sampled-margin limitations. Metadata categories, ratings, prices, stores, review text and simulator traits remain unavailable. Public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps do not establish ownership, purchase readiness or compatibility requirements. Generate full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for twenty real training users, five per category, as required; these do not replace host validation.

Keep the pinned host evaluator unchanged: 200 validation users/category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42. When host outputs permit, report positive ranks, rank-8–12 cases, paired hit/miss transitions and target-versus-tenth-negative margins using the host's tie convention. Bootstrap paired users within each category, using the same resampled indices across conditions and equal category weights, for 10,000 draws with an analysis-only seed-42 RNG; report percentile intervals for category and macro HR@10 differences. Such intervals condition on fitted checkpoints and candidates; they exclude training-seed variability, candidate-sampling variability and adaptive selection bias. Three condition-level observations cannot establish diagnostic predictive validity. Update the embedded predictor writer whenever architecture or padding behavior changes. Deploy exactly one checkpoint per category from the selected condition; never average, fuse, stack or vote across conditions.
idea.pseudocode:
Predeclare A/B/C, p=0.5, alpha=0.5, common E<=200, final-checkpoint selection,
200 batches/epoch, macro selection and tie order A then B then C.
Confirm the complete twelve-run plan fits the remaining charged GPU budget.

For condition in [A, B, C]:
  For category in the four required datasets:
    initialize corrected GRU4Rec and baseline RNG streams with seed 42
    initialize identical dedicated sampling, negative and crop generators
    for epoch in range(E):
      for update in range(200):
        _, sequence, positive, negative = family_specific_sample_batch(...)
        valid = baseline_valid_supervision_mask(sequence, positive, negative)
        keep = zeros_like(sequence, dtype=bool)
        for row with n > 0 nonpadding inputs:
          K = n
          if crop_rng.uniform() < 0.5:
            K = crop_rng.randint_inclusive(max(1, ceil(0.5*n)), n)
          keep[row, last_K_nonpadding_positions] = True
        context = sequence * keep if condition == C else sequence
        supervision = valid if condition == A else valid & keep
        candidates = baseline_candidates_with_B_C_matching(...)
        reset per-example recurrent state
        features = model.log2feats(context)  # skip padded updates; aligned B x L x H
        loss = unchanged_baseline_objective(
            features, positive, candidates, supervision,
            documented_reduction_identical_for_B_and_C)
        update this model using the fixed baseline schedule
    save final checkpoint and consistent predictor artifacts in trial directory
    run charged family-compatible checks and diagnostics
  obtain unchanged host macro validation HR@10 for this complete condition
  record cumulative charged GPU-seconds

Select one condition by macro validation HR@10, breaking exact ties A then B then C.
If paired validation outputs are available, report category and macro paired-bootstrap
intervals conditional on checkpoints and candidates; do not claim seed robustness.
Deploy only the selected condition's four category checkpoints.
At prediction, load exactly one model/category and process full permitted history,
reading the final nonpadding feature with the same padding semantics as training.

originality.positive: The matched-supervision control makes a familiar sequence augmentation more interpretable by separating context removal from target allocation.
originality.negative: Suffix cropping, recency-focused sampling and controlled ablations are established; this is a task-specific experimental design rather than a new model class.

future_potential.positive: A reproducible comparison can guide whether subsequent GRU improvements should address context retention or supervision allocation.
future_potential.negative: Benefits remain unmeasured, and one-seed results cannot establish robustness or distinguish stale-context removal from generic regularization.

code_difficulty.positive: The core change uses input and supervision masks while retaining the GRU architecture and ordinary inference.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct candidate matching, recurrent padding, RNG separation, loss reductions and budget-controlled execution require more care than a simple cropping implementation.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential? An Analysis of Datasets for Evaluation of Sequential Recommendations
contributions: Uses interaction-order perturbations to investigate sequential recommendation benchmarks.
Motivates separating order sensitivity from the influence of recent interactions.
limitations: Does not establish that stochastic prefix removal improves the supplied corrected GRU4Rec.
Perturbation sensitivity alone cannot identify useful historical context.

related_work.title: Recency sampling for sequential recommendation
contributions: Investigates recency-focused training sampling.
Motivates treating target exposure as a separate experimental variable.
limitations: Changing sampled targets differs from removing context while holding supervised targets fixed.
Does not supply results for the proposed three-condition experiment.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can yield comparisons inconsistent with full-catalog evaluation.
Supports distinguishing sampled training diagnostics from the benchmark selection metric.
limitations: Does not determine which proposed condition will perform best.
Does not justify changing the pinned host evaluator.

related_work.title: Contrastive Learning for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Uses sequence augmentations for auxiliary contrastive learning.
Provides related precedent for experimenting with altered sequence contexts.
limitations: Contrastive supervision differs from retaining original next-item targets under suffix cropping.
Does not establish an optimal retained-length distribution for this GRU task.

related_work.title: Recurrent Neural Networks with Top-k Gains for Session-based Recommendations
contributions: Develops ranking losses including BPR-max and TOP1-max for recurrent recommendation.
Highlights the importance of candidate sampling and loss semantics.
limitations: Does not establish which loss the supplied corrected baseline implements.
Its loss definitions cannot substitute for inspecting the actual baseline sampler and reduction.

related_work.title: Official GRU4Rec implementation
contributions: Provides reference implementations of GRU4Rec training, sampling and losses.
Offers implementation context for distinguishing BPR-max from ordinary mean BPR.
limitations: The host's corrected baseline may use different implementation choices.
Reference code does not establish equivalence of the proposed experimental conditions.

related_work.title: PyTorch GRU documentation
contributions: Documents recurrent equations showing that zero inputs can still update hidden state.
Supports explicit handling of padding rather than relying solely on zero embeddings.
limitations: Does not automatically enforce the task's left-padding or aligned-output contract.
Padding correctness must be checked in the actual model and predictor.

related_work.title: PyTorch recurrent sequence packing implementation
contributions: Provides the sequence-packing implementation used to exclude padded recurrent steps.
Supports compacting valid tokens into prefixes before packing internally.
limitations: Left-padded inputs require transformation before ordinary prefix-length packing.
Unpacked features must be restored to original positions for the ModelView contract.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains overfitting of model-selection criteria and resulting evaluation bias.
Motivates predefined configurations, checkpoint rules and transparent selection.
limitations: Predeclaring three conditions reduces flexibility but does not eliminate winner-selection optimism.
User bootstrap intervals do not correct adaptive selection bias.

related_work.title: Accounting for Variance in Machine Learning Benchmarks
contributions: Investigates distinct sources of benchmark variability.
Supports separating user-sampling uncertainty from initialization and hyperparameter uncertainty.
limitations: Does not provide uncertainty estimates for these category models.
The required fixed training seed prevents direct estimation of training-seed variability.

related_work.title: Show Your Work: Improved Reporting of Experimental Results
contributions: Advocates reporting performance in relation to computational search expenditure.
Motivates recording attempted runs and best observed validation performance against budget.
limitations: Does not determine an affordable epoch count for the supplied datasets.
Concurrent execution reduces elapsed time without increasing the shared GPU-time allowance.
